name: ask_user
description:
Ask the user when you genuinely cannot proceed well without their decision: a choice that is theirs to make, a requirement the request leaves open, a trade-off only they can weigh. Do not ask what you can find out yourself by reading the code or running something, and do not ask for approval of an action — the harness does that.

- Ask everything you need in ONE call (up to 4 questions); never a question per call.
- Give 2–6 options per question: the answers you actually think are plausible, each with a short description of what it means. Mark the one you would choose with recommended: true.
- Do NOT add an "Other" or "Something else" option: the user always gets a free-text row, and can also answer with a question back.
- header: a 1–3 word chip label, at most 30 characters.
- multiple: true when several options can apply together.
- Never ask for a password, key or other secret.

The answer comes back as one line per question: "→ label", "→ custom: …", or "↩ counter-question: …". When the user asks a question back, answer it, then ask again — only that question.
